posts.author: Sarah Chen
posts.title: The little Salesforce things that made a big difference this week
posts.body: A cleaner page layout. A flow that saved someone an hour. That one formula finally working. Let’s celebrate the small wins — what’s yours this week?

posts.author: Marcus Johnson
posts.title: I built a free LWC component library. Here’s a first look 👀
posts.body: After rebuilding the same components across projects, I finally put them in one place. Accessible, customizable, and made for the way we actually build on Salesforce. Would love your feedback!

posts.author: Emily Parker
posts.title: What’s one Flow best practice you wish you’d learned sooner?
posts.body: Mine: stop putting everything in a single record-triggered flow. Moving reusable logic into subflows has made debugging so much easier. What would you tell your past self?

posts.author: Daniel Kim
posts.title: From my first agent to an actually useful service assistant
posts.body: I spent the weekend building an agent that looks up case history and suggests next steps. The biggest lesson? Clear topic boundaries matter more than a clever prompt. Here’s what worked, what didn’t, and what I’d try next.

posts.author: Priya Patel
posts.title: Passed my Platform Developer I exam! My study notes and honest advice
posts.body: Three months of early mornings, plenty of practice questions, and a lot of Trailhead. Today it all paid off. My advice: build something small every week. Reading Apex and writing Apex are very different things.

posts.author: Alex Rivera
posts.title: A simple pattern for handling errors in screen flows
posts.body: Every screen flow deserves a useful error message. I’ve been using a shared error-handling subflow that logs the details and gives the user a clear next step. How does your team handle this?
